notes.meaning: God holds good and wise people, along with their actions, safely in His care. Looking only at earthly life, no one can tell whether God is pleased or angry with a person just by seeing whether they are rich or poor. Outward circumstances do not reveal God's eternal love.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Latin Vulgate translates this verse to say that man does not know whether he is worthy of love or hatred, which early church writers applied to our inability to foresee how strictly God will judge our deeds.

notes.meaning: On the outside, the exact same earthly troubles and final death happen to everyone. A faithful person who worships God faces the same earthly hardships as a wicked person who refuses to honor Him. While life's events look the same on the surface, God still sees a profound difference between the righteous and the sinner.

Watching good and bad people meet the same earthly end can deeply trouble the heart. Because wicked people see that all people die alike, they often feel bold to chase their foolish desires without fear. In the end, their wild pursuit of sin leads straight to the silence of death.

As long as someone is alive, there is still reason to hope. In ancient times, dogs were seen as lowly scavengers, while lions were honored as majestic beasts. Yet the poorest living beggar is better off than a mighty king who has died, because the living still have time to turn to God.

Living people know that death is ahead, which gives them time to prepare their hearts. When people die, their earthly career is finished, and they no longer take part in the labors, love, or jealousies of this world. Those left behind soon forget them, showing that earthly fame never lasts.

other.label: Popular modern teaching
other.view: Some groups cite these verses to argue for soul sleep, teaching that human beings lose all conscious existence between death and the resurrection.

notes.meaning: God wants His people to enjoy their daily food and drink with thankful, cheerful hearts. When someone walks in obedience, God welcomes their humble labor and blesses their honest meals. Taking quiet joy in simple provisions is part of living in His favor.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: The Douay-Rheims translation renders the last clause as 'because thy works please God,' viewing it as an assurance that God accepts a person's righteous actions.

notes.meaning: Bright white clothes and olive oil on the head were customary signs of festival joy and clean living. Solomon encourages people not to walk around in gloom, but to embrace a cheerful and neat appearance. Rejoicing in God's everyday gifts honors the One who provides them.

God gave marriage as a sweet comfort to help people through their brief years on earth. A man should stay loyal and treasure the wife he loves each day of his short life. True companionship at home is God's chosen blessing for the hard labor we face under the sun.

Whatever good duty or task you have before you, give it your absolute best effort today. In the realm of the dead, where our bodies will soon rest, there will be no more opportunity to labor, plan, or turn to God. Life is our only window to serve the Lord and care for others.

In this world, the fastest runner does not always win the race, and the strongest soldier does not always win the battle. Even wise and talented people can find themselves without food or honor when unexpected trials arrive. Success ultimately rests in God's hands, so no one should rely only on natural ability.

Human beings cannot predict when sudden trouble, disaster, or death will arrive. Just as fish are caught without warning in a net or birds are trapped in a snare, hard times fall on people unexpectedly. Because life can change in a moment, we ought to live in constant dependence on God.
The writer introduces an example of wisdom that made a lasting impression on his mind. It showed him both the amazing power of wisdom and how easily the world overlooks its true worth.

A mighty king marched with a great army against a small city with very few defenders and surrounded it with siege walls. A poor, wise man inside the city used his good judgment to save everyone from ruin, yet afterward no one remembered to honor or thank him. His mind accomplished what weapons could not, but his low status caused people to ignore him.

Wisdom is far better than brute physical force, because careful thought can solve problems that strength cannot touch. Even so, the crowd often ignores the counsel of a poor person simply because he lacks money and social rank. True wisdom must find its satisfaction in doing right rather than seeking human applause.

Quiet words spoken with calm wisdom have far more power than the loud shouting of a foolish ruler. Boastful leaders rely on noise and bluster to control others, but patient truth eventually wins over reasonable minds. Real wisdom does not need to yell to prove its value.

Wise and godly living is more effective for safety than all the weapons of war. Yet it takes only one rebellious sinner to tear down a vast amount of good work and bring ruin upon a community. While one wise person can bring great blessing, a single corrupt influence can cause widespread harm.
